Related: #34638 — `opencode acp` has the same root cause. Both `serve` and `acp` are non-TUI subcommands that skip the config initialization pipeline used by CLI/TUI mode. In `acp` mode, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, cwd `opencode.json`, and `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` are all ignored — the ACP subprocess uses only `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`.

This blocks tooling that launches `opencode acp` as a subprocess (editors, CI, multi-agent orchestrators like Charon) from injecting per-run provider overrides. The fix for `serve` (PR #23318?) would likely fix `acp` as well if it addresses the shared initialization gap.

Automated review from Aiden's agent.

I found one permission regression introduced by this PR:

- `packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts:127` classifies generic Bash `expansion` assignment values as safe to strip. That lets Bash 4.4+ prompt expansion hide executable work behind an allowlisted command. For example, `EVIL='$(touch /tmp/pwn)' FOO=${EVIL@P} echo hello` parses `FOO=${EVIL@P}` as an `expansion` with no `command_substitution` descendant, so this PR strips the env assignments and permission matching sees only `echo hello`. If the user has an allow rule like `echo *`, the command can be auto-approved while Bash executes the command substitution from the variable value during `${...@P}` expansion.

This is a behavior change from the current implementation: before this PR, the full `EVIL=... FOO=... echo hello` pattern would be evaluated and would not match a simple `echo *` allowlist. I would reject generic `expansion` unless the operator is inspected, or at least specifically reject prompt-transform forms like `${...@P}`.

I also noticed a test-only issue: the new tests at `packages/opencode/test/tool/shell.test.ts:1130`, `:1152`, and `:1174` use `run(..., capture(requests))`, so after the permission request is captured the shell still executes `curl evil.com` through command substitution/backticks/process substitution. That can make CI perform external network calls or hang. Those cases should stop after capture with `capture(requests, err)` plus `fail(...)`, or use a harmless local command.

Closing as not planned for 2.0 after team review.

Decision:

- Keep OpenCode V2 on the existing built-in `node:sqlite` runtime path.
- Do not replace it with upstream `@effect/sql-sqlite-node` / Drizzle Effect SQLite for 2.0.
- The blocker is still native dependency/packaging risk: `@effect/sql-sqlite-node@0.52.0` depends directly on `better-sqlite3` (`^12.6.2`).
- The rc.4 migration attempt in #34674 remains closed/unmerged.

We can revisit upstream Drizzle/Effect SQLite support after 2.0 if it becomes useful, or port isolated safe pieces separately, but this tracker should not stay open as a 2.0 replacement task.

🌍 **Extended RTL support to all RTL languages**

Updated `RTL_LOCALES` in `packages/app/src/context/language.tsx` from only `ar` to include all known RTL-script languages:

| Language | Code | RTL |
|----------|------|:---:|
| Arabic | `ar` | ✅ |
| Persian / Farsi | `fa` | ✅ (ready) |
| Urdu | `ur` | ✅ (ready) |
| Pashto | `ps` | ✅ (ready) |
| Sorani Kurdish | `ckb` | ✅ (ready) |
| Hebrew | `he` | ✅ (ready) |
| Yiddish | `yi` | ✅ (ready) |
| Sindhi | `sd` | ✅ (ready) |
| Uyghur | `ug` | ✅ (ready) |
| Divehi (Maldivian) | `dv` | ✅ (ready) |
| Dari (Afghan Persian) | `prs` | ✅ (ready) |

The `localeDir()` function now checks this map — so when translations for any of these languages are added in the future, the app will **automatically switch to RTL layout** with zero additional configuration. The `rtl.css` styles are already generic and work with any `[dir="rtl"]` attribute. 🚀
